decision.summary: Two regions stand out: (1) a rapid multi-sample offset near index 488–491 in the overlapping window, with coordinated N/E/U shifts suggesting a possible jump or abrupt motion onset; (2) a high-variability segment starting at index 605, featuring large N excursion and complex cross-axis morphology that may indicate superposed or partially reversing changes. Other segments show noisy but monotonic or oscillatory trends without clear morphological anomalies.

regions.observation: Sharp multi-sample rise in N (from ~5.8 to ~7.8) and E (from ~-2.3 to ~-1.5) over 3–4 samples around index 488–491, with U also increasing; appears as a rapid offset rather than smooth motion, possibly a jump or transient platform onset.

Sustained high-amplitude N/E/U variability from ~605 onward, including a prominent N spike to ~10.5 at index 608–609 followed by a drop to ~7.2, with E and U showing correlated but non-symmetric behavior; ambiguous whether this reflects superposed opposing changes or a complex platform with partial return.
